Persistent tracking and fingerprinting across sessions — Tracking networks use cookies, IndexedDB, local storage, and browser fingerprinting to correlate user identity across sessions, undermining privacy guarantees.

Credential and token leakage via session persistence — OAuth tokens, session cookies, and saved credentials persist in browser storage, creating risk of theft if session is compromised or storage not properly destroyed.

Malware attempting to persist across session destruction — Drive-by malware, cryptominers, or persistent XSS payloads attempt to survive session termination by exploiting storage, network callbacks, or browser engine bugs.
Shared endpoint exploitation for session reuse — Attackers on public Wi-Fi or shared workstations attempt to hijack active sessions or extract credentials from endpoint memory or cache.

Unauthorized session creation via control plane compromise — Attacker exploits control plane vulnerabilities or stolen credentials to create unauthorized sessions, bypass rate limits, or disable audit logging.

Session TTL bypass for indefinite session extension — Attacker or compromised user manipulates session lifecycle to bypass TTL enforcement, maintaining long-lived sessions that accumulate tracking data.
Container escape to access other sessions or host system — Attacker exploits container runtime or kernel vulnerabilities to escape isolation, access other sessions, or compromise host infrastructure.

Streaming layer interception exposing browser session content — Attacker intercepts or decrypts video stream to observe user browsing activity, credentials entered, or sensitive information displayed.
Resource exhaustion denial of service — Attacker floods control plane with session requests or maintains excessive concurrent sessions to exhaust compute resources and prevent legitimate usage.

Incomplete session cleanup leaving residual artifacts — Container destruction fails to fully remove ephemeral storage, leaving cookies, cache, or credentials accessible to subsequent sessions on same host.
Browser engine zero-day exploitation — Attacker exploits unpatched browser vulnerability to achieve remote code execution, sandbox escape, or information disclosure within session.
